product.name: PatchPitch
product.description: A local writing workflow that turns selected development facts into drafts for Telegram, X, DEV and GitHub.

audience: Developers preparing announcements for their own projects

facts.text: PatchPitch 0.3.0 is an open-source Python developer tool. Its non-interactive CLI automates local draft generation from JSON/TOML jobs with Ollama, without starting a browser or PatchPitch HTTP server.
facts.limitations: Ollama and an installed local model are prerequisites. The CLI prepares drafts; it does not publish platform announcements.

facts.text: Campaigns retain input snapshots, original model responses and failed attempts on disk. Explicit resume continues unfinished steps; successful steps and edited export files are preserved.
facts.limitations: Changing source data or runtime uses a different run identity. Generation does not establish human editorial approval.

facts.text: The new X path plans each post and selects exactly six tags from a user-supplied catalog with dated observations, topic terms and audience information. The application reserves their length before writing and validates the complete text.
facts.limitations: Missing or stale evidence blocks X rather than inventing popular tags. Matching uses lexical rules and needs meaning review. Length remains a conservative estimate; verify in X.

facts.text: The optional Quillgrain integration can verify an existing bundle or compile an explicitly chosen local pack. Each request checks language, register and channel and keeps the exact voice snapshot.
facts.limitations: The trusted Quillgrain 0.1.0rc3 engine must be installed separately. Structural compatibility is not proof of an authentic author voice.

facts.text: The campaign runner produces Telegram posts, DEV articles and GitHub notes from selected facts. A separate explicit DEV adapter creates or updates a remote draft with published=false and retains a receipt.
facts.limitations: DEV draft delivery needs an API key and always sends published=false. A real account draft/update and separately authorized article publication were completed; unknown-response recovery has offline regression coverage. This candidate workflow does not publish anything.

facts.text:
A real Ubuntu 24.04 headless run of the same inference code returned four accepted drafts with gemma4:12b in 1599.653 seconds using five model requests. Validation, session export and unchanged repeat/resume passed. The exact reproduction command for a prepared checkout is:
```sh
PATCHPITCH_MODEL=gemma4:12b PATCHPITCH_TIMEOUT=600 python -m patchpitch run --job examples/headless/all-four.toml --out-root artifacts/campaigns --json </dev/null
```
facts.limitations: This is one CPU observation of the pre-RC development version, not a benchmark or a fresh 0.3.0 inference run. DEV took 497.921 seconds, so this configuration needs timeout=600. Gemma 3 4B failed this campaign. The dated catalog needs review after 30 days.
